headline: Bethel starter pack.
subhead: A quick run through the local anchors across town. Swipe.

slides.title: Greenwood Avenue downtown
slides.text: The walkable center with local storefronts, the public library, and municipal offices along one main corridor.

slides.title: Huntington State Park
slides.text: Spans over one thousand acres across Bethel, Redding, and Newtown with multi-use trails and ponds.

slides.title: Putnam Memorial State Park
slides.text: Connecticut's oldest state park marks the winter encampment of Continental troops from 1778 to 1779.

slides.title: Bethel train station
slides.text: Located right downtown on the Metro-North Danbury Branch, offering rail connections toward South Norwalk and Manhattan.

slides.title: P.T. Barnum monument
slides.text: A bronze sculpture outside the town library honoring the Bethel native and historic showman.

slides.title: Winter tree lighting
slides.text: A long-running late November gathering along Greenwood Avenue with hot cider and soup around P.T. Barnum Square.

caption:
Bethel CT has a distinct layout that centers heavily around Greenwood Avenue. 

You have an active downtown rail stop, two massive state parks right at the town borders, and Route 6 connecting you straight into Danbury or Newtown. November also brings the annual tree lighting on P.T. Barnum Square, which kicks off the colder months downtown.
